newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND SIGNS 25-YEAR GAS IMPORT DEAL WITH RUSSIA.
newsitem.headline: POLAND SIGNS 25-YEAR GAS IMPORT DEAL WITH RUSSIA.

text.p: Poland signed on Wednesday a landmark 25-year agreement with Russia's giant state-owned gas supplier Gazprom for the supply of 250 billion cubic metres of natural gas.

The contract, signed by Gazprom's president Rem Vyakhirev and head of Poland's Oil and Gas Mining (PGNiG) Aleksander Findzinski, secures gas imports from the large pipeline linking the Yamal Siberian peninsula and Western Europe through Poland.

"This deal is of fundamental importance to our country, it secures energy needed for long-term, stable growth of the Polish economy," PGNiG's Findzinski told reporters before a signing ceremony held at a Warsaw gas plant.
Russia's Vyakhirev said the 25-year deal, the biggest in Europe to date, was an important step for the two countries and would nearly double Gazprom's natural gas exports to Poland.
"In Europe there has not been such a (gas) contract...in the past we sold to Poland about 140 billion cubic metres of gas and today's contract nearly doubles that amount," he said.
"This deal is beneficial for both countries...and it is good for Russia and for Gazprom," Vyakhirev said.
The contract envisages gas imports to gradually increase to 12.5 billion cubic metres per year in 2010.
The Russian gas imports should cover between 30 and 40 percent of Poland's needs in the 1997 to 2010 period, estimated at 22 to 27 billion cubic metres per year.

The deal, which took six years to complete, sparked criticism from some Polish opposition parties, which said that it again made the formerly communist country dependant on natural resources from its large Eastern neighbour.
"This does not endanger our energy security because Poland stood, stands and will stand on coal (energy)," said Poland's Industry Minister, Klemens Scierski, also present.

Natural gas, one of the most environment-friendly energy sources, currently accounts for about 8.5 percent of Poland's energy supply but its share will increase to about 10 percent in the future, Scierski said.
Scierski said Poland would use part of the imports to create a 4.5 to five billion cubic metre natural gas reserve.
He said Poland would soon sign a 180 million ECU deal with the European Investment Bank to finance the construction of large underground gas tanks for the country's reserve.

"We are looking for foreign and primarily for domestic capital...(and PGNiG) will soon sign a 180 million ECU agreement with the European Investment Bank to finance the contstruction of underground gas tanks," Scierski said.
Poland had ealiers said it was in negotiations with Norway and Middle Eastern countries about possible gas imports.
Earlier this year Gazprom began work on a pipeline able to carry 67 billion cubic metres of gas annually from the Yamal penninisula to Germany by 2010.
The pipeline was expected to cost some $2.5 billion.
The value of the Polish-Russian gas deal signed on Wednesday was not disclosed but PGNiG's Findzinski said that Poland would pay less for gas than Western European countries.
